content: Advancements in South Africa’s cybersecurity standards, particularly those concerning data protection and artificial intelligence compliance laws, provide forward-looking insights into the compliance costs that organizations must integrate into their cybersecurity budgets [23] . The impact of these sophisticated phishing attack vectors on South African individuals and organizations is profound and multifaceted. Sub-Saharan Africa is recognized globally as one of the most exposed regions to cyber incidents, driven in large part by persistent gaps in regulation and preparedness, with South Africa frequently listed among nations experiencing severe cyber-enabled fraud [45] . When state infrastructure is compromised, the cascading effects can disrupt essential public services, thereby amplifying the impact of the initial cyber intrusion. Economic diversification in South Africa has also expanded the attack surface across the healthcare, retail, and manufacturing industries [3, 5]. In South Africa, regulatory gaps remain a prominent issue, with slower progress in implementing consistent governance structures compared to more developed international markets [41] . This regulatory lag, combined with the uneven implementation of advanced strategic frameworks such as Zero Trust architecture, leaves critical sectors deeply exposed to both domestic and international threat actors [1, 3]. Addressing these industry-specific vulnerabilities requires comprehensive modernization efforts, enhanced regulatory frameworks, and the deployment of resilient cybersecurity architectures capable of protecting South Africa's critical economic sectors and state infrastructure from an increasingly aggressive global cyber threat landscape. Financial Impact of Phishing and BEC in South Africa The cybersecurity threat landscape in South Africa has evolved into a complex and highly sophisticated environment, characterized by a persistent escalation in malicious activities targeting both the public and private sectors. As the digital economy expands, the vulnerabilities inherent in interconnected systems have been increasingly exploited by cybercriminals utilizing advanced tactics. The financial impact of phishing and Business Email Compromise in South Africa cannot be overstated, as these attack vectors are specifically designed to manipulate human vulnerabilities and bypass traditional perimeter defenses.
